content: All individuals diagnosed with diabetes should undergo an evaluation for diabetic peripheral neuropathy. For those with type 2 diabetes, this assessment should occur at the time of diagnosis. For individuals with type 1 diabetes, the evaluation should take place five years after the initial diagnosis. Following these initial assessments, annual screenings for diabetic peripheral neuropathy are recommended. The assessment for neuropathy should include specific tests to evaluate sensory function. Diabetic neuropathies encompass a wide range of disorders that affect both the peripheral nervous system and the autonomic nervous system. It is important to note that up to 50% of cases of diabetic peripheral neuropathy may be asymptomatic. However, even in the absence of symptoms, the condition can lead to serious complications, such as the development of foot ulcers, if not properly managed. Maintaining optimal glycemic control is essential in slowing the progression of diabetic neuropathy. However, it is important to understand that while good glycemic control can help prevent further damage, it does not reverse existing nerve damage.
